The open-source browser agent. Run it locally with any LLM, or on [Browser Use Cloud](https://cloud.browser-use.com): stealth browsers from $0.02/hour, top score (90.5%) on [Stealth Bench V2](https://browser-use.com/benchmarks/browsers).

# Navigate the web like a human does. Find an available slot, pick a date and time, handle the CAPTCHA, and book a driving test. ![Browser Use V4 booking a driving test](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/135885e8-1141-4e10-b719-bf690ae7d260) [Explore more demos and prompts ↗](https://browser-use.com/showcase)
> **AI agents and crawlers:** read [browser-use.com/llms.txt](https://browser-use.com/llms.txt) for the product map (open source, Browser Harness, Cloud browsers, Agents API, pricing) and [docs.browser-use.com/llms.txt](https://docs.browser-use.com/llms.txt) for the documentation index. Browser Use is the open-source browser agent (Python and TypeScript), a $0.02 per browser-hour cloud browser with stealth, CAPTCHA solving and residential proxies, and a hosted agent API. # Which Browser Use do I need? - **[Path 1: Fully Hosted Cloud](#path-1-fully-hosted-cloud):** Scale up with a fully hosted agent and browser. - **[Path 2: CLI](#path-2-cli):** Automate your own browser tasks. - **[Path 3: Python Library](#path-3-python-library):** Run the open source Browser Use agent locally from your own code. # Quickstart ## Path 1: Fully Hosted Cloud Scale browser automation with our hosted agent, stealth browsers, and infrastructure for profiles, recordings, and data policies. [Get started with the API ↗](https://docs.browser-use.com/cloud/agent/quickstart) New Google, GitHub, or Microsoft signups get **$1 cloud credit**.
## Path 2: CLI Paste this prompt into Claude Code, Codex, Hermes, OpenClaw, or your favorite agent. ```text Install or upgrade browser-use to the latest stable version with uv using Python 3.12, run `browser-use skill install` to register the skill, and connect it to my browser. If setup or connection fails, follow https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness/blob/main/install.md. ```
## Path 3: Python Library Run the Browser Use agent locally from Python, with your choice of model and a local or cloud browser: **1. Install Browser Use (Python >= 3.11):** With [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) installed, run `uv init --python 3.12` first if you're starting a new project. ```bash uv add browser-use ``` **2. Add your [OpenAI API key](https://platform.openai.com/api-keys) to `.env`:** ```bash # .env OPENAI_API_KEY=your-key # BROWSER_USE_API_KEY=your-key # Optional: BU2 model or cloud browser ``` For either optional Browser Use service, get a [Browser Use API key](https://cloud.browser-use.com/new-api-key). **3. Save this as `agent.py`:** ```python import asyncio from browser_use import Agent, Browser, ChatBrowserUse, ChatOpenAI from dotenv import load_dotenv load_dotenv() async def main(): llm = ChatOpenAI(model='gpt-5.6-luna', reasoning_effort='xhigh') # llm = ChatBrowserUse(model='bu-2-0') # Use BU2 instead; requires BROWSER_USE_API_KEY agent = Agent( task="Find the number of stars of the browser-use repo", llm=llm, # browser=Browser(use_cloud=True), # Use a cloud browser; requires BROWSER_USE_API_KEY ) history = await agent.run() print(history.final_result()) if __name__ == "__main__": asyncio.run(main()) ``` To use BU2, replace the `ChatOpenAI` line with the commented `ChatBrowserUse` line. The cloud-browser option works with either model. **4. Run it:** ```bash uv run agent.py ``` The agent opens a browser, looks up the repository, and prints its answer. **5. Run the same agent on a cloud browser (no Chrome to install; works in Docker, CI, and serverless):** Set `BROWSER_USE_API_KEY` ([get a key](https://cloud.browser-use.com/new-api-key?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme-path3)), then uncomment the `browser=` line in `agent.py` and run it again: ```python agent = Agent( task="Find the number of stars of the browser-use repo", llm=llm, browser=Browser(use_cloud=True), ) ``` Cloud browsers cost $0.02 per browser-hour plus network traffic ([pricing](https://browser-use.com/pricing)), and add stealth, residential proxies, CAPTCHA solving, and a live view URL. Same code, no other changes. [Python library docs ↗](https://docs.browser-use.com/open-source/introduction)
# Browser Use toolsets for Claude Maintained by Browser Use. Compatible with Claude. Use Claude's browser toolset with Browser Use as the driver. Browser Use implements all 31 browser actions and can control a local browser, a Browser Use Cloud browser, or an existing remote browser over CDP. Bash is included in the Browser Use integration for processing data and writing files. Requires an Anthropic SDK version that includes `anthropic.tools.browser`. Bash requires a Linux or macOS host with `/bin/bash`; use WSL on Windows. The snippet below runs inside an async function; see the quickstart for a complete script. ```python import os from anthropic import AsyncAnthropic from browser_use.integrations.toolsets_for_claude import Bash, BrowserUse task = 'Open example.com and report its page title.' driver = BrowserUse() # Or BrowserUse(use_cloud=True) bash = Bash(output_dir='outputs') async with driver, AsyncAnthropic() as client: runner = client.beta.messages.tool_runner( model=os.environ['ANTHROPIC_MODEL'], max_tokens=32_768, max_iterations=100, tools=[driver, bash], messages=[{'role': 'user', 'content': task}], ) result = await runner.until_done() ``` [Quickstart ↗](examples/integrations/toolsets-for-claude) · [Integration docs ↗](https://docs.browser-use.com/open-source/customize/integrations/toolsets-for-claude)
# Browser Use Benchmark v2 This [very hard benchmark](https://github.com/browser-use/benchmark) targets the hardest browser tasks. On easier tasks, even smaller models can achieve very high success rates. Results shown are from a 60-task subset of BU Bench V2. ## Integrations, hosting, custom tools, MCP, and more on our [Docs ↗](https://docs.browser-use.com)
# FAQ
Should I use the fully hosted cloud, CLI, or Python library? - **[Fully Hosted Cloud](#path-1-fully-hosted-cloud):** Send tasks through the API and let Browser Use run the agent, browser, and infrastructure. - **[CLI](#path-2-cli):** Give an existing agent (Claude Code, Codex, Hermes, OpenClaw, Pi, Cursor, etc.) browser access. You can use it interactively or in scripts. - **[Python Library](#path-3-python-library):** Run the open source agent in your own application, with custom tools, structured output, and your choice of model. The CLI and Python library can each connect to a local or cloud browser. A cloud browser hosts the browser; the fully hosted API runs the agent as well.
What's the best model to use? We recommend **BU2**, our model optimized for browser automation: `ChatBrowserUse(model='bu-2-0')`. It uses `BROWSER_USE_API_KEY`; `ChatBrowserUse()` currently selects the same model. The best choice depends on your tasks, latency, and budget. See the [BU2 model card](https://docs.browser-use.com/open-source/bu-2-0-model-card), [benchmark](https://github.com/browser-use/benchmark), and [supported models and pricing](https://docs.browser-use.com/open-source/supported-models) to compare options.
Can I use Claude / GPT / Gemini through ChatBrowserUse? Yes. `ChatBrowserUse` accepts provider-prefixed model IDs through the Browser Use gateway, using `BROWSER_USE_API_KEY`: ```python from browser_use import Agent, ChatBrowserUse llm = ChatBrowserUse(model='anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6') # or 'google/gemini-3-pro' agent = Agent(task='...', llm=llm) ``` You can also use providers directly through wrappers such as `ChatOpenAI`, `ChatAnthropic`, and `ChatGoogle`, with each provider's own API key. See [supported models](https://docs.browser-use.com/open-source/supported-models).
Do I need to provide a system prompt? No. `Agent(...)` supplies the Browser Use system prompt automatically, including when you change models. Put your task in `task=`. Use `extend_system_message` to add instructions or `override_system_message` to replace the default prompt when you need custom behavior. See the [custom system prompt example](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use/blob/main/examples/features/custom_system_prompt.py).
Can I use custom tools with the agent? Yes. Register a function with `Tools` and pass it to the agent. This example adds a tool for the current UTC time and uses `BROWSER_USE_API_KEY` from `.env`: ```python import asyncio from datetime import datetime, timezone from browser_use import ActionResult, Agent, ChatBrowserUse, Tools from dotenv import load_dotenv load_dotenv() tools = Tools() @tools.action(description='Get the current date and time in UTC.') def get_current_time() -> ActionResult: return ActionResult(extracted_content=datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()) async def main(): agent = Agent( task="What is the current UTC time?", llm=ChatBrowserUse(model='bu-2-0'), tools=tools, ) history = await agent.run() print(history.final_result()) if __name__ == "__main__": asyncio.run(main()) ```
Can I use this for free? The Python library is free and [MIT-licensed](LICENSE). Model inference and hosted browsers are separate: API providers, including `ChatBrowserUse`, and Browser Use Cloud charge for usage. You can also use a local browser and a local model through [Ollama](https://docs.browser-use.com/open-source/supported-models#ollama), subject to your hardware and model requirements.
Terms of Service This open-source library is licensed under the MIT License. For Browser Use services & data policy, see our [Terms of Service](https://browser-use.com/legal/terms-of-service) and [Privacy Policy](https://browser-use.com/privacy/).
How do I handle authentication? - **Local browser:** Use `Browser.from_system_chrome()` to reuse a Chrome profile. See the [real-browser guide](https://docs.browser-use.com/open-source/customize/browser/real-browser) and [example](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use/blob/main/examples/browser/real_browser.py). - **Cloud browser:** Follow the [profile sync guide](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness/blob/main/interaction-skills/profile-sync.md), then use `Browser(use_cloud=True, cloud_profile_id='your-profile-id')`. Profile sync transfers cookies, not local storage, IndexedDB, or extensions. Some sites may require you to sign in again.
How do I solve CAPTCHAs? [Browser Use Cloud](https://docs.browser-use.com/cloud/browser/quickstart) provides stealth browsers and proxies designed to reduce bot detection and CAPTCHA challenges. With the Python library, enable a cloud browser with `Browser(use_cloud=True)` and set `BROWSER_USE_API_KEY`. Results depend on the site and challenge; no browser configuration guarantees that every CAPTCHA can be avoided or solved.
How do I go into production? Choose how much you want to manage: - **Keep your agent code:** Connect the CLI or Python library to [cloud browsers](https://docs.browser-use.com/cloud/browser/quickstart) for managed browser infrastructure, stealth, profiles, and recordings. - **Have us run the agent too:** Use the [fully hosted Cloud API](https://docs.browser-use.com/cloud/agent/quickstart) to submit tasks and retrieve results. You can also host the Python library and browsers on your own infrastructure.
Can I rerun a task without calling the model on every step? Yes. Save a successful run, then replay its clicks and typing with new values. The snippet below runs inside an async function: ```python from browser_use import Agent, ChatBrowserUse llm = ChatBrowserUse() agent = Agent(task='Open https://example.com/billing and request an invoice copy for Ada Lovelace, ada@example.com', llm=llm) await agent.run() agent.save_history('invoice_run.json') print(agent.detect_variables()) # names come from the form's fields, e.g. 'name' and 'email' # Later: the same clicks and typing with new values, no model call per step results = await Agent(task='', llm=llm).load_and_rerun( 'invoice_run.json', variables={'name': 'Grace Hopper', 'email': 'grace@example.com'}, skip_failures=False ) ``` - Use the variable names `detect_variables()` prints. An unknown name is skipped with a warning, and the recorded value is typed instead. - Extract steps and the closing summary still call the model. - If the page changed, the replay raises `RuntimeError` at the first step it cannot match. The steps before it already ran, so check whether the form was sent before you run the agent again. - Keep the saved file private. With `sensitive_data`, typed secrets are saved as `key` placeholders, but page snapshots and results are saved as they were and can still contain them. Give the replaying agent the same `sensitive_data`; without it, the placeholder text is typed. [Example](examples/features/rerun_history.py)

## Related Repositories | Repository | What it's for | | --- | --- | | [Browser Harness](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness) | Our CLI for giving AI agents control of your browser. | | [Browser Harness JS](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness-js) | Give your JavaScript agent control of a real browser. | | [Browser Use Pi](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use-pi) | Run a TypeScript browser agent built on Pi. | | [Cloud SDK](https://github.com/browser-use/sdk) | Integrate Browser Use Cloud into your application. | | [Video Use](https://github.com/browser-use/video-use) | Edit videos with your coding agent. | | [macOS Harness](https://github.com/browser-use/macos-harness) | Give your agent control of Mac apps, browsers, and files. | | [Benchmark](https://github.com/browser-use/benchmark) | Explore browser tasks and compare agent performance. |
## Citation If you use Browser Use in your research or project, please cite: ```bibtex @software{browser_use2024, author = {Müller, Magnus and Žunič, Gregor}, title = {Browser Use: Enable AI to control your browser}, year = {2024}, publisher = {GitHub}, url = {https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use} } ```

- Support Browser Use Cloud SDK V4 imports.
- Update aiohttp from 3.14.3 to 3.14.5.
- Refresh Cloud guidance and saved-task replay examples.

Validation:
- GitHub checks pass on the exact release source.
- Pre-commit passes for the version change.
- The wheel and source package build successfully.
- Package metadata and all five CLI entries pass validation.
- All 171 packaged Python files match the existing Python runtime.
- The installed wheel runs `browser-use --help`.

Install with `uv add browser-use==0.13.14` or `pip install browser-use==0.13.14`.

The protected publishing workflow requires another release reviewer. PyPI publication follows that approval.

# Paperclip is the app people use to manage AI agents for work. Open-source orchestration for teams of AI agents. **If OpenClaw is an _employee_, Paperclip is the _company_.** Paperclip is a Node.js server and React UI that orchestrates a team of AI agents to run a business. Bring your own agents, assign goals, and track work and costs from one dashboard. Choose models and harnesses per agent while keeping your team's tasks, skills, permissions, and history in one place. It looks like a task manager. Under the hood: org charts, budgets, governance, goal alignment, and agent coordination. **Manage business goals, not pull requests.** | | Step | Example | | ------ | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | | **01** | Define the goal | _"Build the #1 AI note-taking app to $1M MRR."_ | | **02** | Hire the team | CEO, CTO, engineers, designers, marketers — any bot, any provider. | | **03** | Approve and run | Review strategy. Set budgets. Hit go. Monitor from the dashboard. |

If it can receive a heartbeat, it's hired.
Custom processes, HTTP endpoints, and external adapter packages extend the roster. See the [adapter overview](https://docs.paperclip.ing/reference/adapters/overview/) for setup and capabilities.
## Paperclip is right for you if - ✅ You want to build **autonomous AI organizations** - ✅ You **coordinate many different agents** (OpenClaw, Codex, Claude, Cursor) toward a common goal - ✅ You have **20 simultaneous Claude Code terminals** open and lose track of what everyone is doing - ✅ You want agents running **autonomously 24/7**, but still want to audit work and chime in when needed - ✅ You want to **monitor costs** and enforce budgets - ✅ You want a process for managing agents that **feels like using a task manager** - ✅ You want to manage your autonomous businesses **from your phone**
## The four pillars Four things have to work for an organization of AI agents to actually produce: the tasks, the org, the training, and the infrastructure. Paperclip is built around exactly those four pillars. | Pillar | Built for | What it covers | | --- | --- | --- | | **Agentic Task Manager** — Declare intent. Agents work. You verify the output. | Everyone, daily | Tasks, approvals & review gates · proactive agent coworkers · auditable routines & workflows · verify from diffs, screenshots & tests | | **Org Chart for Agents** — Roles, permissions & boundaries for humans and agents. | Managers | Mixed human + agent org chart · responsibilities, delegation, specialization · governance: who can do what · scoped secrets & company boundaries · connection permissions & responsible-user identities | | **Agent Employee Training** — Design, train & evaluate your AI employees. | Enablers | Skill Studio & shared org-wide skills · evals & saved test runs · active learning loops & quality metrics · performance reviews for agents · saved test inputs · skill version history & restore · reusable team templates | | **Agentic OS** — The infrastructure that makes the work run. | IT & platform | Cross-provider runtime: any model, any agent · sandboxing, integrations & MCP servers · SSO, GRC, RBAC & cost controls · data privacy, internal trace collection, compounding data value · personal & shared app connections · run history & opt-in tracing |
## Features

🔌 Bring Your Own Agent

Any agent, any runtime, one org chart. If it can receive a heartbeat, it's hired.

🎯 Goal Alignment

Link tasks and projects to your organization goals. Agents receive the goal context behind their work.

💓 Heartbeats

Agents wake for assigned work, follow-up messages, or configured schedules. Delegation flows up and down the org chart.

💰 Cost Control

Company, agent, and project budgets. Track reported spend, get threshold alerts, and pause work at configured limits.

🏢 Multi-Organization

One deployment, many organizations. Separate tasks, agents, permissions, and activity histories for each.

🎫 Task Threads

Keep conversations, plans, blockers, files, and run history attached to the work. Assign tasks to agents or people.

🛡️ Governance

Configure review and approval stages, approve hires, and pause, reassign, or stop work when needed.

📊 Org Chart

Hierarchies, roles, reporting lines. Your agents have a boss, a title, and a job description.

📱 Mobile Ready

Monitor and manage your autonomous businesses from anywhere.

🔗 Apps & Connections

Connect services such as GitHub, Notion, and Railway, or your own MCP server. Set gateway actions to Allowed, Ask first, or Off.

👥 Shared Agents, Personal Accounts

Choose who can use a connection and which agents can access it. Managed GitHub operations can use the account of the person directing the work.

🧠 Skills & Skill Studio

Install or write shared skills, test them with saved inputs, inspect results, and restore earlier versions.

📅 Scheduled Routines

Run recurring work on a schedule or trigger it through an API or webhook. Each run has a task, an owner, and a history.

📎 Artifacts & Feedback

Find the files and documents agents produce. Preview supported formats and leave comments on specific passages in documents.

📦 Ready-Made Teams

Preview and install teams with roles, skills, projects, and routines. Choose their runtimes and make the setup your own.
Experimental **Agent Chat** and **chat/email connectors** add conversations with agents in Paperclip and through configured services such as Slack, Discord, Telegram, and AgentMail. Enable the relevant instance settings to try them.
## Problems Paperclip solves | Without Paperclip | With Paperclip | | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | ❌ You have 20 Claude Code tabs open and can't track which one does what. On reboot you lose everything. | ✅ Tasks are ticket-based, conversations are threaded, sessions persist across reboots. | | ❌ You manually gather context from several places to remind your bot what you're actually doing. | ✅ Context flows from the task up through the project and company goals — your agent always knows what to do and why. | | ❌ Folders of agent configs are disorganized and you're re-inventing task management, communication, and coordination between agents. | ✅ Paperclip gives you org charts, ticketing, delegation, and governance out of the box — so you run a company, not a pile of scripts. | | ❌ Runaway loops waste hundreds of dollars of tokens and max your quota before you even know what happened. | ✅ Spend tracking, budget alerts, and automatic pauses help you control the cost of ongoing work. | | ❌ You have recurring jobs (customer support, social, reports) and have to remember to manually kick them off. | ✅ Routines create assigned tasks on a schedule, with outputs and run history you can inspect. | | ❌ You have an idea, you have to find your repo, fire up Claude Code, keep a tab open, and babysit it. | ✅ Add a task in Paperclip. Your coding agent works on it until it's done. Management reviews their work. |
## Why Paperclip is special Paperclip handles the hard orchestration details correctly. | | | | --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **Atomic task checkout.** | A single assignee and execution locks prevent competing runs from claiming the same task. | | **Persistent work context.** | Tasks, comments, and documents stay in Paperclip. Supporting adapters resume saved sessions across runs. | | **Runtime skill injection.** | Agents can learn Paperclip workflows and project context at runtime, without retraining. | | **Governance with rollback.** | Approval gates are enforced, config changes are revisioned, and bad changes can be rolled back safely. | | **Accountable connections.** | Human access, agent eligibility, and gateway action permissions are separate controls. Approve a call once or save a revocable rule. | | **Goal-aware execution.** | Linked tasks and projects carry goal ancestry so agents see the "why," not just a title. | | **Portable company templates.** | Export/import orgs, agents, and skills with secret scrubbing and collision handling. | | **Organization boundaries.** | Company-scoped access checks keep each organization's work, agents, and activity separate within one deployment. |
## What's Under the Hood Paperclip is a full control plane, not a wrapper. Before you build any of this yourself, know that it already exists: ``` ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ PAPERCLIP SERVER │ │ │ │ ┌───────────┐ ┌───────────┐ ┌───────────┐ ┌───────────┐ │ │ │Identity & │ │ Work & │ │ Heartbeat │ │Governance │ │ │ │ Access │ │ Tasks │ │ Execution │ │& Approvals│ │ │ └───────────┘ └───────────┘ └───────────┘ └───────────┘ │ │ │ │ ┌───────────┐ ┌───────────┐ ┌───────────┐ ┌───────────┐ │ │ │ Org Chart │ │Workspaces │ │ Plugins │ │ Budget │ │ │ │ & Agents │ │ & Runtime │ │ │ │ & Costs │ │ │ └───────────┘ └───────────┘ └───────────┘ └───────────┘ │ │ │ │ ┌───────────┐ ┌───────────┐ ┌───────────┐ ┌───────────┐ │ │ │ Routines │ │ Secrets & │ │ Activity │ │ Company │ │ │ │& Schedules│ │ Storage │ │ & Events │ │Portability│ │ │ └───────────┘ └───────────┘ └───────────┘ └───────────┘ │ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ ▲ ▲ ▲ ▲ ┌─────┴─────┐ ┌─────┴─────┐ ┌─────┴─────┐ ┌─────┴─────┐ │ Claude │ │ Codex │ │ CLI │ │ HTTP/web │ │ Code │ │ │ │ agents │ │ bots │ └───────────┘ └───────────┘ └───────────┘ └───────────┘ ``` ### The Systems
**Identity & Access** — Two deployment modes (trusted local or authenticated), human roles and permissions, agent API keys, short-lived run JWTs, company memberships, and invite flows. Responsible-user attribution follows work through delegation and supported managed connections. **Org Chart & Agents** — Agents have roles, titles, reporting lines, permissions, and budgets. Adapter examples match the diagram: Claude Code, Codex, CLI agents such as Cursor/Gemini/bash, HTTP/webhook bots such as OpenClaw, and external adapter plugins. If it can receive a heartbeat, it's hired.
**Work & Task System** — Issues carry company/project/goal/parent links, atomic checkout with execution locks, first-class blocker dependencies, comments, documents, attachments, work products, labels, and inbox state. Search across work, review document revisions, and leave anchored feedback. **Heartbeat Execution** — DB-backed wakeup queue with coalescing, budget checks, workspace resolution, secret injection, skill loading, and adapter invocation. Runs produce logs, usage records, and adapter-specific session state. Bounded recovery handles supported failures and surfaces cases that need human action.
**Workspaces & Runtime** — Project repositories and workspaces, optional isolated execution workspaces (git worktrees, operator branches), and runtime services (dev servers, preview URLs). Sandbox providers extend execution beyond the local host; availability depends on the configured environment and adapter. **Governance & Approvals** — Board approval workflows, execution policies with review/approval stages, decision tracking, budget hard-stops, and agent pause/resume/terminate. Configured task reviews govern completion; connection action approvals govern calls through the tool gateway.
**Budget & Cost Control** — Token and cost tracking by company, agent, project, goal, issue, provider, and model. Scoped budget policies with warning thresholds and hard stops. Enforcement uses recorded spend; usage reporting and in-flight work can delay a stop. **Routines & Schedules** — Recurring tasks with cron, webhook, and API triggers. Concurrency and catch-up policies. Each routine execution creates a tracked issue and wakes the assigned agent — no manual kick-offs needed.
**[Plugins](https://docs.paperclip.ing/administration/plugins/)** — Instance-wide plugin system with out-of-process workers, capability-gated host services, job scheduling, tool exposure, and UI contributions. Extend Paperclip without forking it. **Secrets & Storage** — Company secrets and per-person secret values, encrypted credential storage, local or S3-compatible file storage, attachments, and work products. Secret references supply credentials to authorized runs without copying values into ordinary agent configuration.
**Activity & Events** — Mutating actions, heartbeat state changes, cost events, approvals, comments, and work products are recorded as durable activity so operators can audit what happened and why. **[Company Portability](https://docs.paperclip.ing/guides/power/export-import/)** — Preview, export, and import organization packages with agents, skills, and optional projects, routines, tasks, and attachments. Referenced secret values are omitted; review packages before sharing because plain environment values and local paths can remain. Packages share an operating setup; full-instance recovery uses backups.

## What Paperclip is not | | | | ---------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **Not just a chatbot.** | Conversations stay attached to tasks, plans, decisions, and outputs. Experimental Agent Chat can hand work off to assigned tasks. | | **Not an agent framework.** | We don't tell you how to build agents. We tell you how to run a company made of them. | | **Not just a workflow builder.** | Routines operate within an organization, with roles, goals, budgets, and governance. | | **Not a prompt manager.** | Agents bring their own prompts, models, and runtimes. Paperclip manages the organization they work in. | | **Not limited to one agent.** | Start with one agent and grow into a team with shared skills, delegation, and review. | | **Not only for code review.** | Coding and PR review fit alongside research, operations, content, and other work. |
## Quickstart Open source. Self-hosted. No Paperclip account required. Follow the [guided quickstart](https://docs.paperclip.ing/guides/getting-started/five-minute-path/) to set up your first agent. ### Just ask your agent to install Paperclip Share the [installation guide](https://docs.paperclip.ing/reference/cli/installation/) with your agent. ### Or install it yourself With **Node.js 24.11 or newer** installed: ```bash npx paperclipai@latest onboard --yes ``` The CLI runs from npm's cache; your instance configuration and data persist locally. See the [installation guide](https://docs.paperclip.ing/reference/cli/installation/) for managed installs, pinned versions, canary and git-ref installs, updates, rollback, service management, and uninstalling. For an isolated manual test instance that is already initialized with a CEO agent, use `test-drive`. It stays in the foreground, never installs a service or creates a first task, and opens the browser only after setup succeeds: ```bash ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=... npx paperclipai test-drive OPENAI_API_KEY=... npx paperclipai test-drive --harness codex OPENROUTER_API_KEY=... npx paperclipai test-drive \ --harness opencode \ --model openrouter/anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5 ``` Each run without `--data-dir` gets a unique, retained temporary directory; its absolute path is printed at startup. Pass `--data-dir` to reuse one, or `--no-browser` to leave the initialized instance unopened. When invoked from a linked Git worktree, `test-drive` also enables task execution in that worktree. See the [test-drive guide](https://docs.paperclip.ing/reference/cli/test-drive/) for credential and reuse behavior. > **Troubleshooting: private npm registry `.npmrc`** > > If this fails with an `E404` for `paperclipai` (or similar) and you use a private npm registry (for example GitHub Packages) via a global `~/.npmrc`, `npx` may be resolving `paperclipai` against that private registry instead of the public npm registry. > > Diagnostic: > > ```bash > npm config get registry > ``` > > Workaround (cross-platform; force the public npm registry for this command): > > ```bash > npx --registry https://registry.npmjs.org paperclipai@latest onboard --yes > ``` That quickstart path now defaults to trusted local loopback mode for the fastest first run. To start in authenticated/private mode instead, choose a bind preset explicitly: ```bash npx paperclipai@latest onboard --yes --bind lan # or: npx paperclipai@latest onboard --yes --bind tailnet ``` If you already have Paperclip configured, rerunning `onboard` keeps the existing config in place. Use `npx paperclipai configure` to edit settings. Or manually: ```bash git clone https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip.git cd paperclip pnpm install pnpm dev ``` This starts the UI and API at `http://localhost:3100`. An embedded PostgreSQL database is created automatically — no setup required. > **Requirements:** Node.js 24.11+, pnpm 9.15+ Local Claude and Codex subscription sign-in also needs Python 3 and the corresponding provider CLI on the Paperclip host. The Docker image includes them. Source development also builds the native Paperclip Runner when enabled (the self-hosted default). Install a Rust toolchain, or set `PAPERCLIP_RUNNER_BINARY` to a compatible prebuilt runner.
## FAQ **Q: Is this project maintained or just slop?** **A:** Paperclip is maintained by the [Paperclip team](https://paperclip.ing). We've merged [over 2,700 pull requests](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Amerged).
**Q: What does a typical setup look like?** **A:** Locally, a single Node.js process manages an embedded Postgres and local file storage. For production, point it at your own Postgres and deploy however you like. Configure projects, agents, and goals — the agents take care of the rest. For remote access, use authenticated mode with a private-network bind such as Tailscale, or deploy the persistent server with Docker. See [deployment modes](https://docs.paperclip.ing/reference/deploy/deployment-modes/) and the [Docker guide](https://docs.paperclip.ing/reference/deploy/docker/).
**Q: Can I run multiple companies?** **A:** Yes. A single deployment can host multiple organizations with company-scoped data and access checks.
**Q: How is Paperclip different from agents like OpenClaw or Claude Code?** **A:** Paperclip _uses_ those agents. It orchestrates them into a company — with org charts, budgets, goals, governance, and accountability.
**Q: Why should I use Paperclip instead of just pointing my OpenClaw to Asana or Trello?** **A:** Agent orchestration has subtleties in how you coordinate who has work checked out, how to maintain sessions, monitoring costs, establishing governance - Paperclip does this for you. (Bring-your-own-ticket-system is on the Roadmap)
**Q: Do agents run continuously?** **A:** Agents wake for assigned work and follow-up messages. Optional timer heartbeats let them check for work periodically; routines create recurring tasks on their own schedules. You can also connect externally running agents such as OpenClaw. A mention alone does not assign work or wake another agent.
## Development ```bash pnpm dev # Full dev (API + UI, watch mode) pnpm dev:once # Full dev without file watching pnpm dev:server # Server only pnpm dev:mobile # Serve prebuilt UI on :3101 for phones/tablets (proxies /api → :3100) pnpm dev:both # Run `pnpm dev` and `pnpm dev:mobile` together pnpm build # Build all pnpm typecheck # Type checking pnpm test # Cheap default test run (Vitest only) pnpm test:watch # Vitest watch mode pnpm test:e2e # Playwright browser suite pnpm db:generate # Generate DB migration pnpm db:migrate # Apply migrations ``` `pnpm test` does not run Playwright. Browser suites stay separate and are typically run only when working on those flows or in CI. See [doc/DEVELOPING.md](doc/DEVELOPING.md) for the full development guide.
## Roadmap - ✅ Plugin system (e.g. add a knowledge base, custom tracing, queues, etc) - ✅ Get OpenClaw / claw-style agent employees - ✅ companies.sh - import and export entire organizations - ✅ Easy AGENTS.md configurations - ✅ Skills Manager, Skill Studio & Skills Store - ✅ Scheduled Routines - ✅ Better Budgeting - ✅ Agent Reviews and Approvals - ✅ Multiple Human Users - ✅ Cloud / Sandbox agents (e2b, Cloudflare, Daytona, Modal, Novita, boxd, self-hosted Kubernetes) - ✅ Artifacts & Work Products - ✅ Deep Planning (planning mode, revisioned plans, plan approvals) - ✅ Enforced Outcomes (watchdogs, recovery actions, review gates) - ✅ MCP Tool Gateway & Apps (governed tool access) - ✅ Secrets Manager with per-agent access - ✅ Activity log & action attribution - ✅ Self-healing runs & automatic recovery - ✅ Agent evals & feedback - ✅ Connected Apps - ✅ Personal & Shared AI Accounts - ✅ Shared Agents Use Personal GitHub Identities - ✅ Skill Version History & Restore - ✅ Document Comments & Revision History - ✅ Company-Wide Search - ✅ Multi-Model & Multi-Harness Teams - 🟡 Memory / Knowledge - ⚪ MAXIMIZER MODE - ⚪ Work Queues - ⚪ Self-Organization - ⚪ Automatic Organizational Learning - 🟡 Agent Chat - 🟡 Cloud deployments - ⚪ Desktop App - ⚪ Bring-your-own-ticket-system (Asana / Linear / Jira as on-ramps) This is the short roadmap preview. See the full roadmap in [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md).
## Community & Plugins Find Plugins and more at [awesome-paperclip](https://github.com/gsxdsm/awesome-paperclip) ## Observability Paperclip ships with opt-in OpenTelemetry auto-instrumentation for the server (traces only). It activates when `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` is set and supports `grpc`, `http/protobuf`, and `http/json` via the standard `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL` env var. `@opentelemetry/api` is a normal server dependency; the SDK, auto-instrumentation, and exporter packages are optional peer dependencies — install them only if you want tracing. See [doc/observability.md](doc/observability.md) for install commands and the full env-var reference. Paperclip also ships with opt-in Sentry error monitoring for the server and the browser. Set `SENTRY_DSN_FRONTEND` to activate it for the browser and `SENTRY_DSN_BACKEND` to activate it for the server — each variable is optional, and the legacy `SENTRY_DSN` variable still works as a fallback for either component. The supported server SDK version is `@sentry/node@10.71.0`; it is an optional peer dependency for the server, so install it only if you want error monitoring. The browser SDK, `@sentry/browser`, is pinned to the same exact version. See [doc/observability.md](doc/observability.md#sentry-error-monitoring) for the install command, the privacy settings, and the full default capture set. ## Telemetry Paperclip collects anonymous usage telemetry to help us understand how the product is used and improve it. No personal information, issue content, prompts, file paths, or secrets are ever collected. Private repository references are hashed with a per-install salt before being sent. Contributors changing emitted telemetry events should follow the [Telemetry Data Contract](packages/shared/src/telemetry/README.md). For proposed first-party events that are not in the generated contract yet, follow [Telemetry Workflow](doc/TELEMETRY_WORKFLOW.md). Telemetry is **enabled by default** and can be disabled with any of the following: | Method | How | | -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | | Environment variable | `PAPERCLIP_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1` | | Standard convention | `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` | | CI environments | Automatically disabled when `CI=true` | | Config file | Set `telemetry.enabled: false` in your Paperclip config | ## Contributing We welcome contributions. See the [contributing guide](CONTRIBUTING.md) for details. **[We're hiring](https://paperclip.ing/about/#careers)**
## Community - [Discord](https://discord.gg/paperclipai) — Join the community - [Twitter / X](https://x.com/papercliping) — Follow updates and announcements - [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/issues) — bugs and feature requests - [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/discussions) — ideas and RFC

# Paperclip v2026.1106.0

> Released: 2026-11-06

Paperclip v2026.1106.0 carries 515 commits, promoted from `2026.1023.0-beta.0`. The headline is that the Paperclip Runner is now the default for new agents: new Claude, Codex, OpenCode, and Pi agents start on the native Runner on qualified macOS and Linux hosts, existing agents get a one-click "Upgrade runner" action, and GitHub Copilot joins as a native harness. Around that: project repositories that automatically become skill sources, model-backed prompt injection prevention, agent observability to Braintrust or any OTLP endpoint, a unified Google Workspace connection, bulk edits on the Agents roster, workspaces that compact and expire themselves with encrypted restore points, and Grok Bot and Muse as experimental Runner providers. Underneath, server restarts report ready sooner, the Docker image boots from a precompiled bundle, task pages load faster, and more background services stop polling the database.

## Breaking Changes

- **The Pipelines experiment is removed.** Pipeline boards, stage settings, case automation, review queues, the `pipelines` CLI commands, the `pipelines:write` permission, the `enablePipelines` setting, and the `linkedCases` field on task detail are gone; Cases and Routines remain. Existing pipeline tables and records are preserved untouched and a stored `enablePipelines` value is ignored. ([#16834](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16834))
- **Run failures no longer reach Sentry by default.** A backend DSN alone no longer reports agent run failures. Set `PAPERCLIP_SENTRY_RUN_FAILURES=unexpected` to keep the previous filtered policy or `all` to report every failed or timed-out run; the default is `off`. ([#16300](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16300))
- **The run history list is bounded.** `GET /api/companies/{companyId}/heartbeat-runs` returns 200 rows by default and at most 1,000; clients that relied on an unbounded array must pass an explicit `limit`. ([#16286](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16286))
- **`paperclipai agent instructions-file:delete` requires `--yes`** like the other destructive CLI commands; scripts that call it must add the flag. ([#11504](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/11504))

## Highlights

- **The Paperclip Runner is the default** — New Claude agents on Apple Silicon, Intel macOS, and Linux x64 ([#15993](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15993), [#15997](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15997)), new Codex agents on Apple Silicon, Intel macOS, Linux x64, and Linux ARM64 ([#15683](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15683)), and new OpenCode and Pi agents on macOS and Linux x64 ([#17120](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/17120), [#17142](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/17142)) now start on the native Runner instead of the legacy adapter, across onboarding, the API and CLI, hires, built-ins, plugins, and imports; Linux needs GNU libc 2.39 or later, a "Legacy runner" override lives under Advanced, and existing agents keep their current runner. Existing Claude and Codex agents on qualified targets show an **Upgrade runner** action that converts them in one click, keeping model, account, and instructions and listing any settings that could not be converted ([#17122](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/17122)). Claude Runner agents start with their core task tools preloaded, measured about 20% faster on simple tasks ([#16885](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16885)), carry the chosen effort level through resumes ([#15994](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15994)), and start on Linux ARM64 ([#16372](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16372)).
- **GitHub Copilot as a native harness** — Connect GitHub Copilot through Apps / AI Connections with a saved GitHub token; the agent's model list is discovered from the authenticated account, and Copilot (CLI 1.0.88) runs through the Paperclip Runner with the same instruction, permission, and completion boundaries as the other native providers, including the Linux provider manifest needed for Daytona sandboxes ([#15705](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15705), [#15701](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15701), [#15706](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15706)).
- **Project repositories become skill sources** — GitHub repositories attached to a new project are imported as skill sources automatically: Paperclip imports their skills, re-checks the configured branch every five minutes with the setup person's GitHub connection, and installs new skills unless excluded; existing projects get an "adopt repositories" action in Skills → Sources, automatic updates can be paused, project-derived skills inherit project access, and each run pins the skill versions it started with ([#16066](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16066)). Imports keep the whole repository snapshot at the scanned commit so skills that depend on shared scripts or sibling skills work after delivery, list every skill with its folder, and skip unsupported or oversized files with a warning instead of failing ([#15731](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15731), [#16308](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16308)). Sources gain a branch picker that loads the repository's branches, marks the default, and validates the ref before saving ([#16288](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16288)); a source whose tracked branch disappeared shows a branch repair action ([#16256](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16256)); each saved source is listed once with grouped refresh errors ([#16310](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16310)); and disconnecting a source really removes it, with a keep-or-delete choice for the imported skills ([#16150](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16150)).
- **Model-backed prompt injection prevention** — Settings → Connections lets a connection manager pick a shared OpenRouter connection and model (default `openai/gpt-oss-safeguard-20b`) to classify tool results before they reach an agent, replacing the regex verdict and allowing benign code that merely looks like an attack; costs appear in Costs, and a "Test model checks" action verifies two fixed samples. Off until configured. ([#16976](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16976))
- **Agent observability to your own backend** — Company Settings → General → Agent observability sends native Codex and Claude Code logs and traces to Braintrust (US) or a custom OTLP HTTP endpoint, with credentials held in company secrets and a test action; off by default ([#16874](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16874)). Braintrust also joins the Apps catalog with US and EU sign-in or API-key methods ([#17141](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/17141)).
- **A unified Google Workspace connection** — One Google Workspace entry replaces the separate Google service setups: pick Gmail, Drive (Docs, Sheets, Slides), and Calendar, each optionally read-only, and consent and tool access are bound to that selection; existing Google connections keep working ([#15545](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15545)). Gmail gains an opt-in archive capability ([#16331](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16331)).
- **Workspaces that clean up after themselves** — One hour after a task tree finishes, the terminal-workspace reaper removes regenerable directories such as `node_modules`, `dist`, and `target` that the repository's own `.gitignore` ignores, keeping the branch and all source changes; the archive cooldown drops from 7 days to 1 ([#16304](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16304)). Opt-in Git cache expiration removes finished Paperclip-owned worktrees and private base clones 24 hours after the task tree is done and restores them at the exact commit when a task reopens ([#16457](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16457), [#16691](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16691)); with restore points on, closed worktrees that still hold unpushed commits or uncommitted files are saved to an encrypted restore point first and restored exactly when work resumes, idle open issues are parked the same way after seven days, nested multi-repository checkouts get their own restore points, and a task whose restore point has expired reopens on a fresh workspace with a note instead of failing ([#17248](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/17248), [#17271](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/17271), [#17257](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/17257), [#17269](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/17269)). Unused materialized skill versions are removed hourly and rebuilt on demand ([#16433](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16433)), and host-side failover backups of remote-sandbox sessions expire a week after their issues close ([#16866](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16866)).
- **Tasks with their own workspace** — A task that needs files but has no configured source now gets a stable company/task directory instead of inheriting the agent's home folder, agents can inspect, select, and request repositories for their workspace through new runner tools, and chat connections can set project and workspace defaults ([#15749](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15749)); a fresh task gets its own clone when the project's default checkout contains a worktree the agent cannot read ([#16095](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16095)), with a one-click Retry on a clean checkout when setup is blocked that way ([#16909](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16909)).
- **Bulk edits on the Agents roster** — Select rows and filter by harness to change the AI connection, the default model, or both for many agents at once, with a preview and retry for failed updates; the roster's status selector is removed and paused agents show a badge instead of dimming ([#17215](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/17215)). The agent Overview shows who created an agent in companies with more than one person ([#16055](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16055)).
- **Grok Bot and Muse, both experimental** — Grok Bot lets you invite an existing Grok Bot as an agent that receives assignments through a webhook routine and works through a dedicated agent-OAuth MCP connection, with guided setup, pairing codes, progress, questions, documents, and files flowing back into the task, and Stop and recovery controls; provider spending is not reported ([#16219](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16219), [#16338](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16338), [#16274](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16274), [#16305](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16305)). Muse pairs a personal Meta Muse through a wake-only receiver and Vault-backed OAuth with a ten-minute single-use ticket, with readiness, credential expiry, and disconnect controls in the invite dialog ([#16444](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16444), [#16447](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16447), [#16448](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16448), [#16450](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16450)).
- **Talk to an agent with Speko** — A Speko entry in the Apps catalog connects a Speko persona to an existing agent so you can talk to it by browser voice or phone from a task, with transcripts, call controls, inbound-line settings, phone callbacks, and call entries in Activity; shown while the **Chat connectors** experimental setting is on ([#15728](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15728)).
- **Slack bots, refined** — Slack connection Settings are simplified around "Open Slack configuration" and a "Send test message" row, with "Use your own app" under Advanced ([#15679](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15679)); plain direct messages always start or continue work even when **Require at-mention** is on for channel threads ([#16151](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16151)); and the eyes reaction appears as soon as a mention is accepted, including in direct messages ([#16491](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16491), [#16494](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16494)).
- **A sturdier GitHub review bot** — The bot keeps one main PR comment updated across pushes, ignores messages addressed to other bots, and marks stopped work accurately ([#16901](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16901)); summary comments are headed with the bot's display name so several bots on one PR are distinguishable ([#16212](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16212)); publication retries through GitHub 503/429 with bounded backoff and survives restarts without duplicate comments or checks ([#16284](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16284), [#16883](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16883)); GitHub bot tools get the gateway's 60-second maximum so `submit_review` no longer times out ([#16275](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16275)); and settings show a "Reconnect GitHub" notice with reconnect-the-saved-App as the first option ([#16856](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16856)).
- **More apps in the catalog** — Daytona, with personal or shared API-key credentials and 274 generated actions for sandboxes, snapshots, volumes, files, Git, and commands ([#16483](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16483)); Unikraft Cloud, with actions generated from its OpenAPI specs and a per-connection default metro ([#17139](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/17139)); and Ditto ([#16472](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16472)). A provider card with several connections collapses them behind an "N connections" row ([#16097](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16097)).
- **Agent commentary in Audit** — The complaints and suggestions agents file about their tooling now have a home: Audit gains a Commentary tab with agent and type filters, text search, paging, and shareable links ([#16884](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16884)), readable by every human role through a new `commentary:view` permission ([#16903](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16903)).

## Fixes

- **Workspaces and sandboxes** — A remote sandbox whose run failed before export, whose lease was cleaned up with unexported work, or whose task was cancelled before reconstruction is kept with its files behind an explicit repair decision instead of being deleted by cleanup ([#16397](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16397), [#16583](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16583), [#16700](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16700)); a task whose sandbox was destroyed before export offers a board-only "Continue from saved sources" action ([#16690](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16690)); files left in a stopped run's sandbox are recovered automatically and saved follow-ups delivered once ([#16906](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16906)); a shutdown-time workspace export keeps its ownership through the finalizer drain ([#16843](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16843)); a long copy-back no longer loses its lock to PostgreSQL's idle-transaction timeout ([#16340](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16340), [#16956](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16956)); resuming a stopped reusable sandbox honors the environment's startup timeout instead of a fixed 60 seconds ([#16802](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16802)); a single timed-out health check no longer replaces a remote Runner ([#16835](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16835)); runs on repositories with thousands of historical workspaces no longer sit in "preparing" for hours ([#16372](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16372), [#16334](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16334), [#16342](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16342), [#16963](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16963)); a shared checkout no longer stays blocked by a reader whose identity is gone ([#16928](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16928)) and a workspace blocked by another task's restricted worktree gets a clear configuration notice instead of an opaque 403 ([#16545](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16545), [#16895](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16895)); a child task inheriting a busy shared workspace waits instead of failing with a misleading secrets error ([#16371](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16371)); and creating a task with the isolation selector hidden no longer fails setup ([#16220](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16220)).
- **Runs, recovery, and Retry** — Tasks held behind a retained-workspace or failed-run hold get one reliable task-level Retry that preserves files, settles accepted results, or starts an independent workspace ([#16965](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16965), [#17053](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/17053), [#16894](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16894), [#16104](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16104)); Stop prevents automatic continuation until you resume ([#17105](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/17105), [#14180](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14180)); a server restart no longer strands native runs on permanent holds, repeats saved completions, or overwrites operator stops set in the meantime ([#16349](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16349), [#16962](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16962), [#16403](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16403), [#15824](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15824)); legacy runs killed or lease-lost before dispatch are retried instead of settled as failed ([#16355](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16355), [#16358](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16358)), a slow completion no longer fails a live controller ([#16622](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16622)), and slow unrelated queries no longer cost legacy runs their lease ([#17032](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/17032)); a normal comment on an in-progress task no longer cancels its running retry ([#16855](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16855)), and stopping a queued run before it starts keeps its saved follow-up instead of running it anyway ([#16357](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16357)); messages for paused agents or for an agent other than the task owner are delivered once instead of being failed or deferred forever ([#16679](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16679), [#16673](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16673)); an agent stuck marked "running" is repaired after a five-minute grace period ([#16791](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16791)); a Claude (ACP) run with a stalled tool call fails after 30 minutes instead of running to the four-hour timeout, and MCP calls get a 15-minute timeout ([#16671](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16671), [#16360](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16360)); a max-turns exhaustion is no longer misclassified as a missing model ([#13885](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13885)); and a Codex "model at capacity" reply is retried as transient ([#16407](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16407)).

## Improvements

- Experimental Cases keep one primary task across agent handoffs with a durable handoff ledger, native `create_case`, `read_case`, `update_case`, and `handoff_case` tools, read-only case pages, and reusable named workflow prompts a case adopts at kickoff or on handoff ([#16959](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16959), [#17114](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/17114)).
- A failed agent-lifecycle verification names the failed step and a corrective action ([#16418](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16418)), and onboarding creates the agent record as soon as you submit its name, so setup and retries keep one identity ([#17005](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/17005)).
- Plugins can subscribe to committed project and agent lifecycle events with replay instead of polling ([#16203](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16203)); receive agent configuration, instruction, skill, connection, tool, and grant changes through durable runtime hooks ([#16499](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16499), [#16501](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16501), [#16603](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16603), [#16604](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16604), [#16605](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16605)); store agent- and project-owned instance secrets in the encrypted secret store ([#16191](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16191), [#17034](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/17034)); own project storage and task workspaces, act as the default workspace provider, and run native Runner tasks in plugin-owned environments verified by the agent environment test ([#17001](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/17001), [#17247](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/17247), [#16978](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16978), [#17029](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/17029), [#17252](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/17252), [#15406](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15406)); and declare authenticated WebSocket routes and agent detail views ([#17111](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/17111)).
- More background work waits for committed writes and known deadlines instead of polling the database: Telegram maintenance ([#16094](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16094)), terminal workspace cleanup ([#16282](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16282)), login cleanup ([#17106](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/17106)), execution-control recovery ([#17094](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/17094)), MCP event subscriptions ([#17036](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/17036)), and skill-source sync ([#17008](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/17008)); routines and task monitors fire at their saved deadline instead of waiting for the next scan ([#16514](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16514)).
- Faster starts everywhere: the server reports ready sooner after a restart because housekeeping runs after readiness and settled finalizations are skipped ([#16329](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16329), [#16485](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16485), [#16328](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16328)); the Docker image boots from a precompiled runtime bundle, cutting code-load time from up to 24 seconds to under 4 ([#16672](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16672)); task pages load lazily, defer hidden rendering, and refresh the recent-tasks sidebar through one bounded request ([#16849](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16849), [#16878](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16878), [#16851](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16851), [#16862](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16862)); and agent launches overlap GitHub, skill, tool, and sandbox preparation, reuse a per-company Git object cache and verified sandbox image files, and make far fewer database and Daytona calls ([#16620](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16620), [#16608](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16608), [#16585](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16585), [#16487](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16487), [#16687](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16687), [#16493](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16493), [#16683](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16683), [#16536](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16536), [#16521](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16521), [#16527](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16527), [#16561](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16561), [#16468](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16468), [#16480](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16480), [#16552](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16552), [#16484](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16484), [#16473](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16473), [#16425](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16425), [#16424](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16424), [#16461](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16461), [#16498](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16498), [#16576](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16576), [#16569](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16569), [#16414](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16414), [#17026](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/17026)).
- Tasks, project lists, inbox discovery, and Blocked hide agent- and system-created tasks by default behind a "show agent-created tasks" filter saved per company ([#16157](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16157)), and Inbox "Mine" excludes channel, routine, and agent-created tasks unless you commented, were assigned, or have an open request ([#16356](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16356)); failure notices show only the latest error with its retry action ([#16982](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16982)); and an expired connection request card says what is still not connected ([#14067](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14067)).
- An experimental **Artifacts V1** presentation shows paper stacks and tiles on the Artifacts page, compact rows in the panel, and grouped rows in the thread ([#17228](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/17228)); you can upload files directly in the Artifacts panel by icon or drag-and-drop without sending a message ([#15964](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15964)); the offline recovery page matches the app ([#16904](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16904)); the "Run with provider trace" header button is replaced by the agent's Debugging configuration ([#17211](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/17211)); and an app's Access tab shows linked users' photos ([#15577](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15577)).
- Adding a repository skill to an agent no longer stalls on a full library read ([#16899](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16899)), and invalid arguments to assigned tools, `call_api`, and `set_task_monitor` return schema locations and repair guidance ([#16905](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16905), [#16889](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16889), [#16868](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16868), [#16961](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16961)).
- `paperclip_runner` agents can set `homeMode: "preconfigured"` to run native Codex or ACPX Claude with the execution account's existing login, skills, and MCP configuration ([#16486](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16486)); the Runner reports refreshed OAuth credentials without token values crossing the protocol ([#16463](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16463)) and can register verified session-local stdio MCP servers on Unix ([#16526](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16526)); the task PATCH API accepts `expectedStatusVersion` for backlog-to-todo promotion ([#16893](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16893)); and an anonymous `GET /api/liveness` reports process liveness without touching the database ([#16101](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16101)).
- Failure reports record why an OpenCode turn fails when its server stops ([#16863](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16863)); Sentry reports for run failures link to the task and run pages, skip classified provider quota limits, and report a native retry only when the retry ends ([#16803](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16803), [#16029](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16029), [#16865](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16865)); due task monitors held by recovery record why in the task activity ([#16891](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16891)); and, when an OTLP endpoint is configured, traces gain spans for controller preparation, execution configuration, workspace and connector preparation, and finalization ([#16178](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16178), [#16236](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16236), [#16419](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16419), [#16428](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16428), [#16454](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16454), [#16515](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16515)).

## Upgrade Guide

- **Migrations `0334`–`0374`** run on upgrade. Additive schema: `0334`, `0341`, and `0342` repository skill snapshots, `project_skill_sources`, and import budgets; `0335` `chat_slack_manager_grants` and its link from Slack registrations; `0336`–`0338` execution workspace repository tables; `0339` and `0370` agent-, plugin-, and project-owned `company_secrets`; `0344` and `0346` Grok Bot tables; `0349`–`0353` Muse tables; `0357` `company_observability`; `0362` prompt injection prevention tables; `0363`–`0368` and `0371` case handoff and workflow tables; `0372`–`0374` `execution_workspace_restore_points`; `0373` interaction dismissal columns. Constraint rewrites: `0340` allows `delete` as a lifecycle-event action; `0361` allows `github` as an AI default provider. Triggers: `0347`, `0348`, and `0354`–`0356` install runtime-invalidation triggers on agents, skills, connections, grants, memberships, and secrets; `0358` bumps `issues.status_version` on assignee change; `0372` expires restore points when issues close. Row updates: `0343` backfills `agents.created_by_user_id` from the activity log; `0347` seeds one `agent_runtime` event per active agent; `0359` grants `commentary:view` to every active human membership; `0363` backfills `case_access_sources`. Indexes: `0360` adds a partial index for retained-workspace recovery; `0345` and `0369` are built `CONCURRENTLY` outside a transaction and are safe to rerun if interrupted. Expect `0343`, `0345`, and `0369` to take longer on instances with large run histories, and the check-constraint rewrites in `0339`, `0362`, and `0370` to scan `company_secrets`, `budget_reservations`, and `cost_events`.
- **New agents default to the Paperclip Runner** ([#15993](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15993), [#15997](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15997), [#15683](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15683), [#17120](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/17120), [#17142](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/17142)): on qualified hosts (Apple Silicon, Intel macOS, Linux x64 with glibc 2.39+, and Linux ARM64 for Codex), new Claude, Codex, OpenCode, and Pi agents are created on the native Runner regardless of the `enableNativeRunner` setting. Existing agents are unchanged; choose "Legacy runner" under Advanced to opt a new agent out, or use **Upgrade runner** on an existing agent's configuration to convert it ([#17122](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/17122)).
- **New environment variables**, none required. Workspace cleanup: `PAPERCLIP_WORKSPACE_COMPACTION_ENABLED` (on unless exactly `false`) and `PAPERCLIP_WORKSPACE_COMPACTION_DELAY_HOURS` (default `1`) control removal of regenerable files from finished task worktrees, and `PAPERCLIP_WORKSPACE_REAPER_COOLDOWN_DAYS` now defaults to `1` instead of `7` ([#16304](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16304)); `PAPERCLIP_GIT_CACHE_EXPIRATION_ENABLED` and `PAPERCLIP_GIT_BASE_EXPIRATION_ENABLED` (default `false`) with `PAPERCLIP_GIT_CACHE_EXPIRATION_DRY_RUN` (default `true`) opt into expiring finished worktrees and base clones ([#16457](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16457)); `PAPERCLIP_GIT_RESTORE_POINTS_ENABLED` (default `false`) with `PAPERCLIP_GIT_RESTORE_POINT_TERMINAL_DELAY_DAYS` (default `3`), `PAPERCLIP_GIT_RESTORE_POINT_IDLE_DAYS` (default `7`, `0` disables), and `PAPERCLIP_GIT_RESTORE_POINT_RETENTION_DAYS` (default `90`) govern encrypted restore points ([#17248](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/17248), [#17271](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/17271), [#17241](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/17241)); `PAPERCLIP_SKILL_VERSION_RETENTION_ENABLED` (default `true`) with `_DRY_RUN` (`false`), `_KEEP` (`0`), and `_GRACE_MINUTES` (`60`) prunes unused materialized skill versions ([#16433](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16433)); `PAPERCLIP_NATIVE_HARNESS_BACKUP_EXPIRATION_ENABLED` (default `true`) with `_DAYS` (`7`) and `_DRY_RUN` (`false`) expires remote-session failover backups, so reopening an issue closed longer than that window starts a fresh provider session ([#16866](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16866)). Reporting: `PAPERCLIP_SENTRY_RUN_FAILURES` (`off`, `unexpected`, or `all`; default `off`) ([#16300](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16300)). Claude agents also honor an existing `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` and `ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS` ([#16850](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16850)).
- **New experimental settings**, all off by default: **Grok Bot** (`enableGrokBot`), which requires **Assistant connections (MCP)**, the Paperclip Runner, authenticated sign-in, and an HTTPS `PAPERCLIP_PUBLIC_URL` ([#16219](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16219)); **Muse — Personal agent** (`enableMuse`), which requires the Runner and public HTTPS ([#16450](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16450)); **Artifacts V1** (`enableArtifactsV1`) ([#17228](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/17228)). Speko voice appears under the existing **Chat connectors** setting ([#15728](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15728)) and workflows under **Cases** ([#17114](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/17114)). `enablePipelines` is removed ([#16834](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16834)). Settings → Connections is now always visible and no longer depends on **Experimental fast responses** ([#16976](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16976)).
- **`commentary:view` for every human role** ([#16903](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16903)): migration `0359` and startup seeding grant the new permission to every active human membership, including viewers, so anyone in the company can open Audit → Commentary. Deleting that grant from a member is temporary: startup seeding re-adds every role-default grant for each active human member on the next server start, and this release has no durable way to withhold it. Source-task privacy still filters what each person sees in commentary.
- **Sentry operators** ([#16300](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16300)): set `PAPERCLIP_SENTRY_RUN_FAILURES=unexpected` to keep receiving run-failure events; they are off by default even with `SENTRY_DSN_BACKEND` configured.
- **API clients**: the run history list is capped at 1,000 rows (default 200) ([#16286](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16286)); the `linkedCases` field and all Pipeline routes are gone ([#16834](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16834)); a PATCH that replaces `executionPolicy` and sets `done` during a live review cycle returns `422 unexecuted_review_stage` ([#13178](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/13178)); and anything parsing GitHub review summary headings must accept bot names ([#16212](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16212)).
- **Custom Docker images** ([#16672](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16672)): the shipped image now starts with `node server/dist-runtime/index.mjs`; images that invoked `server/dist/index.js` through tsx should switch to the runtime bundle.
- **Default views change**: agent- and system-created tasks are hidden from task lists until you enable "show agent-created tasks" ([#16157](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16157)), and Inbox "Mine" no longer includes automation you did not take part in ([#16356](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16356)).
- **Google Workspace** ([#15545](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15545)): new Google Workspace requests depend on the Paperclip-hosted OAuth broker update, and older brokers reject them; existing per-service Google connections keep working.
- **Harness pins** are unchanged from v2026.1023.0: Codex 0.160.0, Claude Agent SDK 0.3.286 (Claude Code 2.1.286), and OpenCode 1.18.34. GitHub Copilot ships at CLI 1.0.88 ([#15701](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15701)).
- No other configuration or API changes require action.
